name: Excalibur prefabricated housing
description: Factory-made Uni-Seco house components were transported as kits and assembled on a London housing estate.

date.basis: The date applies to this documented case, not to the worldwide origin of the capability.

events.statement: Historic England dates the estate to 1945–46, describes prefabricated panels and says the estate comprises 187 houses.

evidence.supports: Historic England dates the estate to 1945–46, describes prefabricated panels and says the estate comprises 187 houses.

events.statement: The Housing (Temporary Accommodation) Act authorized up to £150 million for temporary houses nationally.

evidence.supports: Historic England reports national authorization of up to £150 million.
Historic England attributes the 1944 authorization to the national legislation.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest researched operational or depicted case for this record, not a claim of global priority.

caveats: The national budget authorization was not the expenditure on this estate. The site’s assembly workforce is known from residents’ recollections.

research.note: Independent review checked the Historic England listing, the 187-house estate and national spending authorization; the latter was not estate expenditure.
